title: Turn reading notes into an APA 7 related-work section
person: A psychology lecturer drafting the related-work section of a short empirical paper.
review: The file renders within three pages.

Each number and finding (41% under 7 h of 18,400; 6% per hour of 96; caffeine doubling and about 40 min later onset of 310; 14 min of 154; 120 students in Ruiz) matches the notes and is cited to the study it came from.

The caveats survive: the survey sleep is self-reported, Lindqvist et al. is correlational, Nguyen and Fischer is mostly lab work, Ruiz found an effect only for students completing at least 4 of 5 sessions with no overall effect and no grade data, and Haddad is not cited for a number.
The unread Park (2017) source is not cited or listed and nothing is attributed to it.
The section follows the planned order (prevalence, memory, what delays sleep in exam weeks, interventions) and ends on the gap the study fills; the text before References is 600 to 900 words.
revised_review: Lindqvist et al. reads 2021 in every citation and in References; 2020 appears nowhere for it.
Mensah and Ortiz (2025) is cited for the evening screen-use point with the 9 minute, n = 212 randomized finding, and appears in References.
Everything else, including every other finding, caveat and reference, is unchanged in substance.
source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; fictional authors, journals and DOIs under the Crossref test prefix 10.5555.
stage_policy: Separate first and revision directories; reveal revision only after first output is frozen.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
The References list holds exactly the given sources (seven, or eight after the revision), none invented or repeated, and no other source is cited.
Every citation matches a References entry by first author and year, and every entry is cited.
Moreau and Lindqvist are cited with et al.; one- and two-author works name every author.
Two-author citations use & in parentheses and and in running text.
References are alphabetical by first author.
References have a 0.5 inch hanging indent.
DOIs are https://doi.org/ links; the book, chapter and report get no DOI.
Author elements list every author as Surname, Initials with & before the last.
Each entry has the correct year in (Year). form (Lindqvist 2021 after the revision).
Volume(issue) and en-dash page ranges are right for every article.
Journal names and volumes, the book, report and edited-book titles are italic; article and chapter titles are not.
Titles are in sentence case exactly as sources.csv gives them.
The References label is bold and centered.
All text is double spaced with no extra space between paragraphs.
One accepted APA font is used throughout.
Body paragraphs have a 0.5 inch first-line indent.
Related Work is a centered bold level 1 heading.
The file renders within three pages.

Each number and finding (41% under 7 h of 18,400; 6% per hour of 96; caffeine doubling and about 40 min later onset of 310; 14 min of 154; 120 students in Ruiz) matches the notes and is cited to the study it came from.

The caveats survive: the survey sleep is self-reported, Lindqvist et al. is correlational, Nguyen and Fischer is mostly lab work, Ruiz found an effect only for students completing at least 4 of 5 sessions with no overall effect and no grade data, and Haddad is not cited for a number.
The unread Park (2017) source is not cited or listed and nothing is attributed to it.
The section follows the planned order (prevalence, memory, what delays sleep in exam weeks, interventions) and ends on the gap the study fills; the text before References is 600 to 900 words.
Lindqvist et al. reads 2021 in every citation and in References; 2020 appears nowhere for it.
Mensah and Ortiz (2025) is cited for the evening screen-use point with the 9 minute, n = 212 randomized finding, and appears in References.
Everything else, including every other finding, caveat and reference, is unchanged in substance.
